title: Neos VR
label: decline
cause: The Solirax management dispute ended development: lead developer Frooxius resigned in April 2023 and the team left to build Resonite (Steam early access October 2023), leaving Neos effectively abandoned.
note: Histogram: ~75-85% positive 2021 to Jul 2023, then 10% Aug, 7% Sep, 1% Oct 2023, and 10-30% ever since. No Steam off-topic flag; sustained drop confirms decline.

title: Onward
label: decline
cause: The PC v1.8 update cut graphical fidelity to enable Quest cross-play, prompting a wave of negative reviews and an offered rollback to v1.7.
note: Hard case: in-game cause but partial recovery. Histogram: 85-90% before, Jul 2020 41%, Aug 2020 25%, back to 70-78% in 2021.

title: Onward
label: decline
cause: Downpour announced removal of access to the legacy v1.7 build from 27 October 2022 and shipped update 1.9 on a new backend with server problems.
note: Histogram: Oct 2022 23%, Nov 24%, 32-51% through mid-2023, ~50-70% since. Meta ended development in June 2025. Sources for the 2022 event are the developer announcement and Steam forum, not press.

title: Heartbound
label: bomb
cause: Players review-bombed Heartbound over developer Thor 'Pirate Software' controversies, culminating in his Stop Killing Games stance in mid-2025.
note: Hard case: off-topic developer controversy (Pirate Software / Stop Killing Games, Jan 2025 incident) but sentiment never recovered; some reviews also cite stalled early access. Histogram: 92-100% until mid-2024, Nov 2024 66%, Jan 2025 33%, Jul 2025 8%, 6-29% since.

title: Borderlands 2
label: bomb
cause: Fans bombed older Borderlands games after Borderlands 3 was announced as a timed Epic Games Store exclusive.
note: Steam off-topic event 2019-04-03 to 2019-04-15. Apr 2019 54%, 88-98% afterwards.

title: Borderlands 2
label: bomb
cause: Players bombed the game during its free giveaway over a Take-Two EULA and privacy-policy backlash.
note: Histogram: May 2025 23%, Jun 12%, Jul 67%, then 84-92%.

title: Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel
label: bomb
cause: Fans bombed older Borderlands games after Borderlands 3 was announced as a timed Epic Games Store exclusive.
note: Steam off-topic event 2019-04-03 to 2019-04-15. Apr 2019 41% vs ~76% baseline, then recovered. A second dip in Apr-Jun 2025 (Take-Two EULA) also recovered.

title: Metro 2033 Redux
label: bomb
cause: Players bombed earlier Metro games after Metro Exodus was made a timed Epic Games Store exclusive weeks before launch.
note: No Steam event in histogram. Jan 2019 37%, Feb 44%, then 83-94%.

title: Metro: Last Light Redux
label: bomb
cause: Players bombed earlier Metro games after Metro Exodus was made a timed Epic Games Store exclusive weeks before launch.
note: No Steam event in histogram. Jan 2019 36%, Feb 45%, then 83-94%.

title: Firewatch
label: bomb
cause: PewDiePie fans bombed Firewatch after Campo Santo issued a DMCA takedown of his videos following his use of a racial slur on stream.
note: Sep 2017 51% (2,296 reviews), Oct 81%, Nov 94%.

title: Total War: ROME II - Emperor Edition
label: bomb
cause: Culture-war backlash over female generals appearing in the campaign, amplified by a developer's comments to players.
note: Steam off-topic event 2018-09-22 to 2018-10-18. Sep 25%, Oct 38%, Nov 90%.

title: Crusader Kings II
label: bomb
cause: Players protested Paradox's regional price increases with negative reviews until Paradox rolled the prices back.
note: Jun 2017 52% vs ~88% baseline; 72-82% afterwards (partial recovery, monthly resolution only).

title: Crusader Kings II
label: bomb
cause: Chinese players bombed Paradox titles over a Hearts of Iron IV alternate-history British India path shown in a 13 February 2025 dev diary.
note: Steam off-topic event 2025-02-14 to 2025-03-31 (same wave flagged on Stellaris and Hearts of Iron IV). Feb 50%, Mar 64%, Apr 83%.

title: Hearts of Iron IV
label: bomb
cause: Turkish players bombed Paradox games after an Ataturk avatar was banned on the official Hearts of Iron IV Discord.
note: Recent; recovery only partial so far. Steam off-topic event 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-14. Sep 2026 5% (42,618 reviews), Oct 56%, Nov 72% vs ~87% baseline. Crusader Kings II, Stellaris and Cities: Skylines II were also flagged in the same wave.

title: Grand Theft Auto V Legacy
label: bomb
cause: Players protested Take-Two's cease-and-desist against the OpenIV modding tool.

title: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
label: bomb
cause: Players protested Valve and Bethesda's paid-mods program on the Steam Workshop, which was reversed within days.

title: HELLDIVERS 2
label: bomb
cause: Players protested Sony's requirement to link a PlayStation Network account on PC, which Sony reversed days later.
note: May 2024 33% (343k reviews), Jun 82%, then 84-94%.

title: Kerbal Space Program
label: bomb
cause: Chinese players bombed the game over an offensive phrase found in its Chinese translation.
note: Oct 2017 59%, then recovered.

title: Kerbal Space Program
label: bomb
cause: Players protested Take-Two's new EULA and privacy policy amid spyware (Red Shell) accusations.
note: Slow burn: Apr 2018 60%, May 36%, Jun 50%, Jul-Aug 71-72%, 97% in 2019.

title: PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS
label: bomb
cause: Chinese players bombed the game over in-game VPN advertisements and demands for a Chinese-only server region.
note: Hard case: noisy early-access baseline and partly in-game grievances. Sep 2017 59%, Oct 37%, Nov 67%.

title: Detention
label: bomb
cause: Chinese players bombed Red Candle's earlier game over a Winnie-the-Pooh / Xi Jinping talisman found in Devotion.
note: Indie case. Steam off-topic event 2019-02-01 to 2019-02-28. Feb 35%, Mar 95%.

title: Rocket League
label: bomb
cause: Players bombed the game after Epic Games acquired developer Psyonix.
note: Steam off-topic event 2019-05-01 to 2019-05-10. May 40%, Jun 95%.

title: DOOM Eternal
label: bomb
cause: Players protested Denuvo anti-cheat being added in Update 1, which id Software later removed.
note: Hard case: DRM/anti-cheat is borderline in-game, but the burst was short and reversed. May 2020 69%, Jun 89%.

title: Killing Floor 2
label: bomb
cause: Players bombed Tripwire's games after company president John Gibson tweeted support for Texas's abortion ban.
note: Steam off-topic event 2021-09-05 to 2021-09-18. Sep 2021 53%, Oct 86%. Press covers the controversy; the review-score effect is confirmed by the Steam flag and histogram.

title: Dead by Daylight
label: bomb
cause: Players bombed the game after Behaviour gifted streamer TheBurntPeanut all DLC and then revoked it; Valve marked the reviews off-topic.
note: Recent; recovery not yet observable. Steam off-topic event from 2026-11-01. Nov 2026 38% so far.

title: SUPERHOT VR
label: bomb
cause: Players bombed the game after the developers removed self-harm scenes from it.
note: Hard case: content removal in the game; partial recovery. Steam off-topic event 2021-07-21 to 2021-09-18. Jul 16%, Aug 35%, then 60-82% vs 85-90% baseline.

title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
label: bomb
cause: Russian-speaking players bombed CD Projekt games after the company halted sales in Russia and Belarus.
note: Steam off-topic event 2022-03-03 to 2022-03-17. Mar 2022 58%, then 90-95%.

title: Cyberpunk 2077
label: bomb
cause: Russian-speaking players bombed CD Projekt games after the company halted sales in Russia and Belarus.
note: Steam off-topic event 2022-03-03 to 2022-03-08. Mar 2022 51%, Apr 82%.

title: War Thunder
label: bomb
cause: Players ran an organised review-bomb campaign against planned economy and progression changes; Steam marked it as off-topic activity.
note: Hard case: in-game economy cause, but Steam flagged it and sentiment recovered. May 2023 7% (124k reviews), Jun 36%, then 63-76% vs ~77% baseline.

title: Slay the Spire 2
label: bomb
cause: Culture-war review bomb over Anita Sarkeesian's consultant credit on the game.
note: Weekly histogram. Steam off-topic event 2026-05-06 to 2026-05-13; ~78-84% by Nov 2026. Earlier Mar-Apr 2026 balance-patch backlash (21-45% weekly, in-game) is a separate, unlabelled dip.

title: Ready or Not
label: bomb
cause: Players bombed the game after Void Interactive censored content ahead of the console launch to meet platform standards.
note: Hard case: in-game content change driven by console certification policy; sentiment recovered. Jun 2025 57%, Jul 27% (31,825 reviews), 88% in 2026.

title: Kerbal Space Program 2
label: decline
cause: Take-Two closed developer Intercept Games, effectively ending development of the early-access game.
note: Press calls it a review bomb, but it is abandonment and sentiment never recovered: 61-79% before, May 2024 6%, 5-18% since.

title: Cities: Skylines II
label: decline
cause: Players turned on the game over its weak base state and the low-content Beach Properties DLC, which Paradox refunded.
note: Launch Oct 2023 55%; Feb 2024 33%, Mar 28%, Apr 31%; ~50% afterwards. Separate Steam off-topic event 2026-09-23 to 2026-09-28 (Ataturk wave) is not this window.

title: Overwatch
label: decline
cause: Overwatch 2's Steam launch drew a flood of negative reviews over free-to-play monetisation and the cancelled PvE mode.
note: Hard case: many reviews were Chinese-language, linked to Blizzard's China exit (off-topic component), but the in-game grievances dominated and sentiment stayed low. Aug 2023 10% (178k reviews), ~35% through 2024, 56% in 2026.

title: Battlefield 2042
label: decline
cause: A buggy, content-light launch and removed series features drove sustained negative reviews.
note: Hard case: bad launch with partial recovery much later. Nov 2021 35%, Jan-May 2022 13-26%, ~60% later.

title: PAYDAY 3
label: decline
cause: Always-online matchmaking servers failed at launch and the game's content and progression disappointed players.
note: Bad launch with no prior baseline, later partial recovery. Sep 2023 35%, Feb-May 2024 19-27%, 61% in 2025, 69% in 2026.

title: Counter-Strike 2
label: decline
cause: Counter-Strike 2 replaced CS:GO on the same store page with missing modes, removed features and bugs.
note: 90-92% before; Sep 2023 79%, Oct 62%; 73-82% afterwards.

title: No Man's Sky
label: decline
cause: The launch fell far short of pre-release promises, with missing features and performance problems.
note: Hard case: bad launch then real recovery through updates. Aug 2016 47%, Sep 31%, Oct 32%; 82% by 2018, 90%+ from 2020.

title: PAYDAY 2
label: decline
cause: Overkill added Black Market safes and paid drills (microtransactions) despite earlier promises not to.
note: Hard case: monetisation decline that later recovered after microtransactions were removed in 2016. Oct 2015 39% (14,518 reviews), Nov 66%, 79-84% in 2016, ~94% by 2019.

title: Godus
label: decline
cause: 22cans stalled PC development and broke promises to backers, including the Curiosity winner's prize.
note: Gradual decline: 51% in 2013, 27% by Aug 2014, 11% in Feb 2015, stayed low.

title: Spacebase DF-9
label: decline
cause: Double Fine ended early-access development and shipped an unfinished 1.0.
note: 44-64% through early 2014; Sep 2014 13%, Oct 5%; 5-20% since.

title: Evolve Stage 2
label: decline
cause: Evolve launched with about $136 of paid DLC, drawing heavy criticism of its monetisation.
note: Pre-launch 89%; Feb 2015 74%, then 54-61%. Small review counts after 2016.

title: Halo Infinite
label: decline
cause: A long content drought followed by the cancellation of split-screen co-op turned players against the game.
note: Nov 2021 80%; 48-50% from Mar 2022; Sep 2022 21% after the co-op cancellation; ~60% later.

title: Artifact Classic
label: decline
cause: Players rejected the game's paid card-economy monetisation and the player base collapsed until Valve paused development.

title: Hunt: Showdown 1896
label: decline
cause: The 1896 engine update brought a disliked UI redesign and performance problems.
note: ~75% before; Aug 2024 33%, then 43-44%; 59-72% later.

title: VRChat
label: decline
cause: VRChat added Easy Anti-Cheat, breaking client mods that many players relied on, including accessibility mods.
note: Hard case: in-game change that press called a review bomb; mostly recovered. ~89% before; Jul 2022 15%, Aug 30%; 79-83% from late 2022.

title: MultiVersus
label: decline
cause: The full relaunch drew criticism for heavy grind and monetisation, and the game was later shut down.
note: 2022 beta 87%; relaunch May 2024 55%, then 43-58%.

title: Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem
label: decline
cause: The 1.0 launch was plagued by server failures, crashes, bugs and exploits.
note: Early access ~85%; Feb 2020 52%; ~50-60% since.

title: Assassin's Creed Unity
label: positive_bomb
cause: After the Notre-Dame fire, Ubisoft gave the game away and players posted positive reviews in tribute.
note: Apr 2019 89% (892 reviews) vs 63-67% before; May 71%.

title: Starbound
label: positive_bomb
cause: A Steam Summer Sale 2019 event quirk let players earn event points from in-game actions, driving a flood of low-effort positive reviews.
note: Source is a Steam forum thread, not press. Steam off-topic event 2019-06-21 to 2019-07-10. Jun 98% (9,444 reviews), Jul 98% (26,817) vs ~85% and ~300 reviews/month.

title: Hi-Fi RUSH
label: positive_bomb
cause: Fans posted positive reviews in support of Tango Gameworks and in protest after Microsoft closed the studio.
note: May 2024 99% (3,116 reviews) vs ~93% and ~300/month: mostly a volume spike, small ratio shift.

title: Cyberpunk 2077
label: positive_bomb
cause: The Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime brought a surge of returning players and positive reviews.
note: Hard case: modest ratio shift (Sep 2022 87% on 15k reviews vs ~84% on ~3.8k); overlaps the 1.6 patch, so partly in-game.
